title: Wringer fleet scope
description: A `wringer.fleetscope.v1` document — `scope.json` in a fleet bundle: which criteria each task proved, which gates those resolved to, and which bound criteria no task claimed. Written at the START of a scoped fleet, before any child spawns, so a fleet killed mid-flight still says what it set out to prove. It is a RECORD and never an instruction: nothing reads it back, and the scope it describes came from `fleet.scope` in `.wringer.yaml`, which a human wrote (SPEC_SCOPE_V0 ruling 1 — the values are criteria ids, never gate ids, and no model ever sorts a criterion into a task). This file is the machine-readable third of the record; the run bundle's `summary.md` carries the human-readable 'Scoped out' section, and the absent gate results are the third — the one that actually refuses, because acceptance reads absence as `gate-did-not-run`.

fleet_id.description: The fleet bundle this scope belongs to.

declared_gates.description: Every gate `.wringer.yaml` declared, in declared order, AS THIS RUN SAW IT. Present so a reader computes any task's EXCLUDED gates from this file alone — `declared_gates` minus that task's `gates` — rather than having to fetch the config at that commit. A scoped bundle that could not say what it left out would be a narrower claim wearing a full one's clothes.

tasks.description: One entry per task in the fleet's task file. The map is TOTAL when it exists: a fleet where some children are scoped and some run the whole gate set would make 'succeeded' mean two different things in one summary table, and `wring fleet` refuses that before any child spawns.

task.description: The task id, as it appears in the fleet's task file.

criteria.description: The criteria this task proves, in the PM's vocabulary — the ids a human approved in `wringer.spec.yaml`. Never empty: a task with nothing to converge on is refused by name.

gates.description: The gates those criteria resolved to, through the `proves:` bindings already installed in `.wringer.yaml`. One join, declared twice nowhere. Never empty — a task resolving to no gates is refused before the fleet starts.

unclaimed_criteria.description: Bound criteria no task claimed. LEGAL and loud: nothing refuses here, because the operator's final unscoped `wring verify` runs their gates anyway — and if nobody built them those gates go red there, acceptance records it, and `wring deliver` refuses exactly as it does today. Listed so the gap is visible before the fleet runs rather than discovered after it.
